title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (with the previous page): Grothendieck is applying his theory of p-divisible (Barsotti–Tate) groups and their deformations, the subject of the May 1966 letter to Tate, to moduli of polarized abelian varieties. The previous page states the key structural fact. In the 'formal moduli' situation with p-divisible groups N, N' of multiplicative type (ordinary case), the formal moduli variety of extensions is a formal group of multiplicative type over the base A. In Serre–Tate language: for an ordinary abelian variety A_0 over a perfect field k of characteristic p, the formal deformation space is Hom_Zp(T_pA_0(k) ⊗ T_pA_0^t(k), Ĝ_m), a formal torus of dimension g^2.

This page applies that fact to the moduli scheme M of g-dimensional abelian varieties with a given polarization (of degree d) and a Jacobi (level-n) rigidification, in characteristic p, at ordinary points.

(1) Lifting the polarization λ is the closed condition q(x, λy) = q(y, λx) for x, y in T_pA_0. This is the kernel of a homomorphism of multiplicative-type formal groups Ĝ_m^{g^2} → Ĝ_m^{g(g-1)/2}. It is dual to the character map Λ^2 T → T ⊗ T^t, x∧y ↦ x⊗λy − y⊗λx. So the local ring of M at an ordinary point is the coordinate ring of a formal group of multiplicative type.

(2) Consequences stated on the page:
- M is a (local) complete intersection; the word 'lisse' is struck out and replaced.
- M is locally irreducible, because a formal group is connected.
- More precisely M_red is smooth over k ('rigide' is struck and replaced by 'lisse sur k'), since the reduced part of a multiplicative formal group over a perfect field is a formal torus.
- The non-reducedness ('multiplicités') comes from p-torsion in the cokernel of the character map. This can occur only when p divides the degree of the polarization.

(3) Dimension. Lifting ('remontant') to characteristic 0 and using the char-0 theory, the dimension of the modular scheme (with multiplicities) is g(g+1)/2 at every point; equivalently, the character map has finite cokernel, so the dimension is g^2 − g(g−1)/2.

(4) Hence if the polarization degree is prime to p, the modular scheme in characteristic p is smooth (and, presumably, of the generic dimension). The N.B. restricts all of this to ordinary abelian varieties.

The marginal note (hard to read) seems to warn that the dimension count must be checked/indicated when the degree is divisible by p. The problem served: the local structure of the moduli schemes of polarized abelian varieties with level structure in characteristic p, via p-divisible groups and Serre–Tate theory.
errors: No mathematical error. The smoothness conclusion is only claimed at ordinary points, and the N.B. explicitly restricts to ordinary abelian varieties; in the non-ordinary locus nothing is proved here.
'Locally irreducible' should be read as formally/analytically unibranch at ordinary points, which follows from connectedness of the formal group; this is stated, not proved.

The dimension statement g(g+1)/2 'en chaque point' via lifting to char 0 implicitly uses the existence of lifts. For ordinary points this is the canonical lift, so it is fine; for general points it would be a nontrivial claim (cf. later Norman–Oort).

ideas.what: At an ordinary point, the formal local moduli of a polarized abelian variety (with level structure) is a formal group of multiplicative type: the kernel of the symmetry condition inside the Serre–Tate torus Hom(T_pA ⊗ T_pA^t, Ĝ_m).
ideas.modern_name: Serre–Tate canonical coordinates / deformation theory of ordinary polarized abelian varieties
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre–Tate (1964, Woods Hole); written up by Katz, 'Serre–Tate local moduli' (1981); Messing (1972)
ideas.where_published: Possibly sketched in Grothendieck's ICM 1970 talk / 'Groupes de Barsotti–Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné' (1974) only in general form; not as this moduli statement

ideas.what: Consequence: at ordinary points the moduli scheme in characteristic p is a local complete intersection, locally irreducible, with M_red smooth; it is possibly non-reduced (multiplicities) when p divides the polarization degree.
ideas.modern_name: local structure of A_{g,d,n} ⊗ F_p along the ordinary locus
ideas.usually_credited_to: Norman–Oort (Annals 1980, 'Moduli of abelian varieties'); Oort's later work on non-principal polarizations

ideas.what: The dimension of the modular scheme is g(g+1)/2 at each (ordinary) point, by lifting to characteristic 0; so if the polarization degree is prime to p, the moduli scheme is smooth at ordinary points.
ideas.modern_name: smoothness of A_{g,d,n} over Z[1/dn] at ordinary points / dimension of Siegel moduli
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mumford (GIT, 1965) for the existence and dimension; Oort, Norman–Oort for char p

ideas.what: Use of the term 'rigidification de Jacobi' for level-n structure.

missed.claim: Already in 1966, Grothendieck had the Serre–Tate / multiplicative-formal-group description of the ordinary locus for arbitrary (not necessarily principal, degree possibly divisible by p) polarizations. From it he drew the explicit conclusions: local complete intersection, locally irreducible, M_red smooth, dimension g(g+1)/2 with possible multiplicities. This anticipates Norman–Oort-type statements and the non-principal case of Katz's account.
missed.quote: est une intersection complète, et de plus est loc. irréductible, plus précisément M_red est lisse sur k ... la dimension des schémas modulaires (multip.) est bien g(g+1)/2 en chaque point
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents Grothendieck's early use of Barsotti–Tate deformation theory for moduli of polarized abelian varieties with p | degree. The mathematics itself is now standard folklore (formal group of multiplicative type ⇒ lci with smooth reduction).

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, correct application of the Serre–Tate / multiplicative-formal-group description to moduli of polarized abelian varieties in char p, including the non-principal case with multiplicities. It is essentially known through Serre–Tate, Katz and Norman–Oort. Its interest is the early date (1966) and Grothendieck's authorship, not new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: the insertion above '(donnée)' likely reads '(d'échelon n)', i.e. 'rigidification de Jacobi (d'échelon n)'.
Line 4: the insertion is likely 'lisse sur k' (not 'lisse mod k').
Line 6 likely begins 'remontant en car. nulle et utilisant la ...' rather than 'variété ordinaire en car. nulle'.
The insertion over 'schémas modulaires' likely reads 'multipl.' (multiplicités), referring to the possibly non-reduced structure.
The marginal note is largely illegible; the reading 'dimensionnalité indiquée, si la variété divisible en car. p' is doubtful. It may concern the case where the degree is divisible by p.
Line 10: possibly 'degré premier à p et dans le cas général' rather than 'dans le car. générique'.
